glm.feedback:
### Findings

- **Category: spec | Severity: medium**
  **File:** `client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeedCard.tsx` (the `prDuplicateText` / `showText` block)
  **Finding:** Item 1 specifies suppressing *a sentence* that duplicates the PR box title — implying sentence-level stripping. The implementation only suppresses when the **entire** `card.text` equals the synthesized `Merged as "X".` string. If the narrative text is `"Investigated the flaky test. Merged as \"X\"."` (duplicate sentence plus other real content), the duplicate sentence still renders. Conversely, the "near-exact" tolerance from the AC (e.g. trailing-whitespace or period variants) is also unimplemented.
  **Suggestion:** Split `card.text` into sentences (or match the duplicate as a substring with a regex tolerant of punctuation/whitespace) and strip only the matching sentence, rendering the remainder.

- **Category: edge-case | Severity: medium**
  **File:** `client/src/external/session-parser.ts` (`extractTaskNotification`, cap widened 4096→65_536)
  **Finding:** The original failure mode (a multi-KB report silently failing the `endsWith` check, leaving the subrunner card stuck on "running" forever) was not fixed, only moved: any notification whose envelope exceeds 64 KB now returns `null` at the very first line, so the event is dropped entirely and the card is permanently stuck on `"running"` with no report. The Confidence Calibration section itself documents reports that "ran several KB," so this is a realistic input class, not hypothetical.
  **Suggestion:** On oversized content, don't bail before parsing — at minimum still extract `status`/`task-id`/`summary` (truncating `result`) so the card resolves; the `startsWith`/`endsWith` envelope check can also be relaxed (e.g. `lastIndexOf("</task-notification>")`) so a trailing newline or truncated tail doesn't kill the whole event.

- **Category: bug | Severity: low**
  **File:** `client/src/styles/mission-operation.css` (`.mc-feed-pr-meta > span:first-child { flex-shrink: 0; }`)
  **Finding:** The spec says "the PR-number span gets `flex-shrink: 0`". The implementation pins whichever span happens to be the *first child* of `.mc-feed-pr-meta`. This is positional and fragile — a JSX reorder of the merge-state/PR-number spans (or insertion of a new leading span) silently pins the wrong element, reintroducing exactly the clipping this item fixes. Add a test or a dedicated class.
  **Suggestion:** Give the PR-number span its own class (e.g. `.mc-feed-pr-num`) and target that instead of `:first-child`.

- **Category: test | Severity: low**
  **File:** `client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeed.test.tsx` (session-start divider test)
  **Finding:** The divider test only asserts the time portion (`toLocaleTimeString`) is present, and never checks the date/"Today" segment, the "Session started ·" prefix, or that the divider appears *above* the first card. A broken `formatSessionStart` that returns only a time string, or a divider rendered at the bottom, still passes.
  **Suggestion:** Assert the full rendered text (e.g. via a fixed fake-timers date so "Today, 09:15" is deterministic) and assert the divider precedes the first card entry.

- **Category: edge-case | Severity: low**
  **File:** `client/src/components/external/mission/SubrunnerPanel.tsx` (`useEffect` with `[card.subrunnerId]` dep capturing `document.activeElement`)
  **Finding:** If `card.subrunnerId` changes while the panel is open (the reducer can overwrite it mid-lifecycle), the capture effect re-runs and overwrites `returnToRef` with the panel's own close button, so focus is restored to a dead element on unmount rather than the original trigger. Minor a11y regression path, not a crash.
  **Suggestion:** Only capture on mount (empty dep array), or guard against capturing an element inside the panel.

### Notes on what's solid

The reducer wiring is well-designed and matches the spec's corrected mechanism: provisional `tool_use.id` → ack-overwritten stable `agentId` → `taskId`-correlated `task-notification`, with the synchronous-`Task` fallback, the anchored `AGENT_ID_RE`, and the running-card-preference collision handling all implemented and directly unit-tested (including a genuine end-to-end reducer test through `parseSessionJsonl`). Items 2, 4, 5, and 6 are implemented as specified with reasonable test coverage. No security issues found — untrusted report text flows only through `MarkdownChunk` (same as all other transcript-sourced text) and remains React-text-child inert elsewhere.

**Overall:** ship-with-fixes — the core feature is sound and well-tested; fix the sentence-level dedup gap (spec AC1) and the oversized-notification stuck-on-running edge before release; the rest are low-severity hardening.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

openai.feedback:
- Category: spec | Severity: medium | File: `client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeedCard.tsx:252` — Finding: Resolved subrunner cards show the same “View subrunner report” button whether they succeeded or failed. The required done/failed status is invisible. Suggestion: Render distinct done and failed labels or indicators, and test both states.

- Category: spec | Severity: medium | File: `client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeedCard.tsx:58` — Finding: PR dedup works only when the entire `card.text` exactly equals the generated sentence. A near-exact variant, or that sentence within a longer narrative, remains duplicated despite the acceptance criterion. Suggestion: Remove only the matching sentence from rendered text while preserving every other sentence and any `textFull` content.

- Category: bug | Severity: medium | File: `client/src/lib/missionActivityFeedSubrunner.ts:146` — Finding: Every notification status except `"failed"` becomes `"done"`. The parser supplies `"unknown"` when `<status>` is absent, so a malformed notification can falsely mark a running agent complete. Suggestion: Resolve only recognized terminal statuses; leave unknown or nonterminal statuses running.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: low | File: `client/src/external/session-parser.ts:716` — Finding: A valid final report that makes the notification exceed 65,536 characters is discarded wholesale, leaving its subrunner card running indefinitely. Suggestion: Parse the envelope and retain the full report through a size-aware path, or surface an explicit oversized-report failure.

The feature’s main path is implemented and tested, but the status display and completion handling need fixes before shipping. **Ship with fixes.**
